messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: Active p99 SLO breach for streaming generation API in us-west-2 detected at 2026-03-14T11:05:55Z. Paging @leah-oncall.

leah-oncall: acknowledged, I'm on. any customer-side impact reports?

support-bot: 5 open tickets mentioning 'stream freeze' and 'partial responses then hang'. Affected tenants: ad-network, live-chat, ai-analytics. First reports ~10:58Z.

remi: metrics snapshot: p95 ~680ms, p99 jumping to ~12.3s, tail long-tail and streaming stalls visible on trace waterfall. heatmap -> us-west-2 nodes show heavy skew.

kai: runtime logs show repeated kernel ioctl timeouts and nv-host resets. nvml reports Xid 79 and repeated 'GPU has fallen off the bus' entries for GPU device on host gpu-node-42.

infra-bot: node telemetry: gpu-node-42 reporting rising corrected ECC counts and 1 uncorrected ECC. Thermal spikes recorded. Recent events:

```
Mar 14 10:59:10 gpu-node-42 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:68:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 14 11:00:33 gpu-node-42 kernel: nvidia: GPU 0 thermal throttling engaged; temp=91C
Mar 14 11:01:05 gpu-node-42 kernel: NVRM: Uncorrectable ECC error detected on GPU 0
```

remi: pods hosting streaming workloads are colocated on gpu-node-42 and gpu-node-45; p99 is dominated by pods on node-42.

leah-oncall: prioritize: 1) isolate node-42 (cordon+drain) 2) apply routing fallback to quantized variants and cross-AZ spill 3) force-delete pods stuck on socket close 4) lower kernel hang timeout to drop stuck kernels earlier.

kai: running isolation now:

```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=25
```

infra-bot: drain started: evicted 14/20 pods; 6 pods remain in Terminating due to open streaming websockets.

tz-dev: for the Terminating pods I'm seeing preStop waiting on flush ack. I'll try to gracefully close connections, then fallback to forced deletes for the stubborn ones.

```
# forced cleanup for blocked stream pods
kubectl delete pod <pod> --force --grace-period=0
```

remi: after forced deletes and cordon, p99 dropped from 12.3s -> 1.6s within ~3 minutes. p95 ~620ms. Streaming stalls largely stopped.

leah-oncall: routing change: shifting 25% traffic to us-west-1 and enabling fallback variant quant-small-2 for 35% of streaming sessions. DevEx confirmed compatibility for chunked streaming with degraded quality for a subset of clients.

kai: runtime diagnostic on gpu-node-42 before we power it down:

```
# nvidia-smi -q | egrep 'ECC|Temperature|Perf'
Ecc Mode                     : On
Ecc Errors                   : Corrected: 31 Uncorrected: 1
GPU Current Temp             : 92 C
Performance State            : P2

# dmesg | tail -n 8
[  987.654321] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:68:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1002.111213] nvidia: GPU 0 thermal throttling prevented further scheduled work
```

infra-bot: uncorrected ECC + off-the-bus + thermal throttle = hardware-level flake. Marking node-42 for RMA and immediate removal from scheduling.

leah-oncall: also applying runtime config change to reduce kernel hang timeout from 120s -> 40s to avoid long kernel stalls backing up queues.

```
# runtime patch applied
streaming:
  kernel_hang_timeout_seconds: 40
```

tz-dev: patch rolled, rolling restart of runtime workers in region completed in ~90s.

support-bot: notifying affected customers: "We've detected a hardware GPU fault on a host causing streaming stalls. We've failed over traffic to fallback variants and cross-AZ capacity; some customers experienced degraded responses for ~10-25 minutes. We're replacing the faulty hardware and will provide a postmortem." (tickets updated)

remi: monitoring: p99 now ~1.5s, 99.9th ~2.4s, no new ECC/unresponsive events in last 10m after isolation.

leah-oncall: next steps: 1) RMA gpu-node-42 (INFRA-5203) 2) fleet-wide ECC scan and consider auto-taint when uncorrected ECC > 0 3) postmortem with NVML/Xid/dmesg logs, pod stack traces, routing changes, customer impact numbers.

ops-miguel: taking postmortem lead and RMA coordination. I'll work with hw-team for replacement and schedule a firmware sweep for GPUs in us-west-2.

leah-oncall: handing oncall to @ops-miguel for follow-ups. I'll add incident timeline and close when postmortem doc is filed. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident resolved for active SLO breach at 2026-03-14T11:39:15Z. Suspected root cause: flaky GPU with uncorrected ECC + thermal throttling on gpu-node-42. Postmortem owner: ops-miguel (INFRA-5203).
